children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--ICE Futures canola contracts were weaker with speculative selling a feature as values dipped below nearby chart support.
November canola was down 4.10 Canadian dollars at C$807.60 per metric ton on Thursday, hitting its lowest levels since late August.
Losses in Chicago soybeans accounted for some spillover selling pressure, and European rapeseed and Malaysian palm oil were also lower.
However, soyoil futures were stronger at midday.
Seasonal harvest pressure remained a bearish influence, although anecdotal reports that yields and quality may not live up to earlier expectations provided some support.
The Manitoba canola harvest was 86% complete in the latest provincial report, while 89% of the Saskatchewan canola was off the field as of Oct. 12.
An estimated 61,500 canola contracts traded as of 12 p.m. EDT.
